💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Black Friday is here, which means winter riding season is right around the corner.
  • Of course, Black Friday is also a great time to save on cycling gear: Whether you’re buying clothing or equipment for winter rides, shopping for holiday gifts, or upgrading your bike for next spring’s rides, now is the best time to score substantial deals on almost any type of component, accessory, or apparel you need.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. How we test gear.

Black Friday is here, which means winter riding season is right around the corner. For many cyclists, that brings colder temperatures and shorter daylight hours—some of us will boot up Zwift and hit the indoor trainer, while others will tough out the weather on the road and trails.

Of course, Black Friday is also a great time to save on cycling gear: Whether you’re buying clothing or equipment for winter rides, shopping for holiday gifts, or upgrading your bike for next spring’s rides, now is the best time to score substantial deals on almost any type of component, accessory, or apparel you need. Many cycling brands jumped the gun and debuted their Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals a few days early. Plus, almost every big online retailer—including favorites like Amazon, REI, and Backcountry—has a Black Friday sale.

Below is a curated selection of Black Friday gear deals; many of these were editor-tested on the road, trail, or bike commutes. So much great gear is on sale across so many categories that it’s impossible to list everything here. If you don’t see exactly what you need, check out the deal hubs below for top online cycling gear and bike retailers, plus links to sales from leading clothing brands and bike companies. Bookmark this page and return for updates as even more deals come online.

➜ AMAZON ➜ REI ➜ BACKCOUNTRY ➜ COMPETITIVE CYCLIST ➜ BIKE TIRES DIRECT ➜ PERFORMANCE ➜ JENSON USA ➜ PEARL IZUMI ➜ VELOCIO ➜ CAPO ➜ ORNOT ➜ WAHOO ➜ ZWIFT ➜ GARMIN ➜ SPECIALIZED ➜ TREK ➜ CANNONDALE ➜ AVENTON ➜ LECTRIC ➜ VELOTRIC.

Bike lights are a must-have item for anyone commuting or riding road or gravel in the winter months. Even if you already have a light, I’ve found it super useful to own an extra set to have at the office, on my other bikes, or as spares for friends.

Lezyne consistently makes great front and rear lights. While slightly pricier than budget picks found on Amazon or AliExpress, they’re durable, work well, and last several seasons. Plus, we’ve found Lezyne’s advertised runtimes and lumens are much closer to reality than many no-name lights.

Garmin’s Varia RTL515 is our benchmark cycling radar, and its latest RearVue 820 builds on that great reputation—and it’s on sale for Black Friday. Compared to the 515, the RearVue 820 has more battery life (up to 15 hours), a brighter flashing light (100 lumens), and greater vehicle-detection range (up to 191 yards). Plus, the 820 adds a brake-light feature that increases rear light intensity as you slow.

Recent findings suggest that crucially, the RearVue 820 incorporates features found on no other radars (from Garmin or any other brand). While other radars often drop vehicles when they slow down behind you, the 820 tracks vehicles traveling at your same speed; it’s a handy feature you don’t know you need until you try it. Additionally, if you use a Garmin Edge X40- or X50-series computer, the radar tracks a vehicle that changes lanes behind you. It also indicates icons to indicate each vehicle’s size (small, medium, or large).

It has been revealed that showers Pass makes our best-tested winter gloves, and they’re currently on sale at 19% off. In their review, our test rider said, “This knit, waterproof glove has a midweight feel and sufficient insulation when temperatures hover around freezing. Most riders will find the Crosspoints reach its limit at about 30-35 degrees, depending on how hard you’re riding.”.

According to recent reports, the glove traps some body heat, so your fingers may be slightly chilly at first but will warm up within 15 minutes. Better yet, when the mercury climbs, your hands won’t feel hot and sweaty.

Gore’s Endure glove is a solid pick for those cold or wet winter rides. The gloves’ Gore-Tex membrane sheds moisture while Primaloft insulation keeps your hands cozy. The Endure features a textured silicone palm—it helps you hold the bar in slippery conditions. Plus, the gloves are touchscreen-compatible, so you can operate your cell phone or head unit without your hands getting cold.

According to recent reports, shoe covers are a bit like gloves for your shoes. Winter socks help keep your feet warmer on cold rides, but they add bulk that can affect shoe fit. So, many cyclists turn to shoe covers and booties to wear over their cycling shoes. Shoe covers also block wind and create an air barrier to insulate your feet. I’m a fan of Capo’s knit shoe covers—they’re perfect for chilly rides when heavy booties are overkill. (Use code “BLACKFRIDAY25” at checkout.).

Electric mini-inflators burst onto the scene a couple of years ago and have swiftly become a rider favorite for pumping up your tires at home, at the trailhead, or on rides. Of the inflators we’ve tested, the AS2 Ultra came out on top. With svelte dimensions and a 106-gram weight, the Ultra is small enough to stash in a jersey pocket, flat kit, or bar bag. Plus, it quickly inflates tires of all sizes to pressure. The AS2’s super-accurate gauge also makes it worth considering for your home shop or carrying in a race-day tool kit.

RockBros’ inflator stands out for its consistency and is a favorite of Bicycling editors. It’s compact, lightweight, and has an accurate gauge. In our testing of 15 electric pumps, it inflated a road tire to 65 psi in 45 seconds, and filled five tires before running out of power.

The Wahoo Kickr Core 2—Bicycling’s Best Overall Indoor Trainer—is on sale for the lowest price we’ve seen: $399.99. The Core combines excellent performance, great accuracy, and high max resistance in a package perfect for Zwift rides after work, winter training, and even competitive virtual racing.

Indoor training bikes are quickly gaining popularity for their ease of use and low maintenance. With a dedicated indoor setup, you no longer have to wrestle with getting your bike on or off the smart trainer, which also makes it convenient to share with other riders in your family. Plus, you won’t wear out pricey parts. Zwift’s Ride is our favorite: it sets up quickly and adjusts for a wide range of rider heights and fits. It also costs thousands less than its competitors.

Shorter daylight hours and lower temps often mean fewer hours spent riding outside on the road or trail. An indoor trainer helps you maintain your fitness through the winter months while getting your riding fix. Garmin’s Tacx Flux2 is the brand’s mid-range smart trainer; with 2,000 watts of resistance, it simulates gradients up to 16%. The Flux also connects to virtual platforms like Zwift and Rouvy for immersive indoor riding experiences.

Stainless bottles have become popular among cyclists over the past several seasons. They keep water chilled on hot rides and don’t give your water a funny plastic taste. Many gravel and off-road riders love CamelBak’s Stainless Podium, particularly for its open/closed twist-lock cap. The Podium Stainless also ranked best in our heat testing last summer and performed well in our winter bottle testing.

SUMMER BOTTLE TESTING WINTER BOTTLE TESTING.

Sources indicate that with a five-star rating and 8.14 STAR score, the P2R A20 Mips places third in Virginia Tech’s road helmet rankings (and eleventh overall). That ranking is great for any road or gravel helmet—but for a helmet that normally costs only $60, it’s downright amazing.

In a recent development, P2R somehow hits the A20’s low price without cutting many corners on features. It has nice straps with adjustable quick clamps that offer plenty of adjustment. P2R also includes a USB-rechargeable light that magnetically clips into the rear vent for commuting or extra visibility on the road. The one downside we found with the A20 Mips is that it feels optimized for rounder head shapes. While it fits me well, a couple of others who tried it remarked the A20 fits a little snug near their temples.

TOP 5 RANKED VA TECH ROAD HELMETS.

Elite road and gravel helmets offer low weight, excellent ventilation, and great looks. However, those benefits usually come at a high cost. Giro’s Agilis Mips helmet is a great option if you want a pro-level look and performance without the associated price.

Weighing 299 grams (size medium), my Agilis is only 15 grams heavier than Giro’s premium Aries Spherical model—and the Agilis costs significantly less. The Agilis is very well-ventilated, comparable to the priciest lids on all but the hottest of rides.

This helmet features Mips technology to protect your brain from rotational forces in a crash, and Giro’s Hardbody co-molded shell to better protect it from small bumps and dings when not on your head. Plus, the Agilis uses the Roc-Loc dial system to ensure a proper fit.

Recent findings suggest that MET’s Trenta 3K Carbon is one of the top five road helmets by Virginia Tech’s helmet lab. It’s also one of the best for racing and high-performance riding, as proven by UAE Team Emirates’s results—Tour de France champion Tadej Pogačar and World Champion Brandon McNulty. While UAE riders often race the Italian brand’s Manta aero helmet, they pick the lightweight, well-ventilated Trenta 3K Carbon for climbing stages and training.

Unlike some modern helmets with similarly strong protection, the Trenta feels light and racey on your head, and almost disappears when you’re riding. The straps offer good adjustability, and the Mips Air Node liner protects without feeling bulky. However, the Trenta’s biggest drawback is its price tag. Typically priced over $500, this is an expensive piece of kit, but this deal cuts the cost by almost a third.

➜ AMAZON ➜ REI ➜ BACKCOUNTRY ➜ COMPETITIVE CYCLIST ➜ BIKE TIRES DIRECT ➜ PERFORMANCE ➜ JENSON USA ➜ PEARL IZUMI ➜ VELOCIO ➜ CAPO ➜ ORNOT ➜ WAHOO ➜ ZWIFT ➜ GARMIN ➜ SPECIALIZED ➜ TREK ➜ CANNONDALE ➜ AVENTON ➜ LECTRIC ➜ VELOTRIC.

Arm warmers are among the most versatile pieces of cycling clothing you can own. This magical piece of kit turns your short-sleeve jersey into a long-sleeve in seconds—and you can change back to short sleeves again mid-ride if the temps rise.

I’ve owned many pairs of arm warmers over the last three decades, and I rarely ride without them on my arms or in my jersey pocket if the temperatures are between 45 and 60 degrees. Pearl Izumi makes some of my favorites, and these Elite Thermal arm warmers are a steal for the price. They’re easy to pull on or off while riding, and they don’t sag.

Sources indicate that A quality rain jacket is a must-have item for riders who live anywhere it rains or snows. Rapha’s Core Rain Jacket is a great option for layering over your winter jersey without adding too much bulk. It features a two-way zip to regulate body temperature, reflective hits for riding after dusk or in the early morning, and packs down small if the weather clears mid-ride.

If you ride in temps below 40 degrees, a good cycling jacket is a great asset. As a Scottish brand, Endura knows a few things about riding in the cold, dark days of winter, and its MT500 Freezing Point jacket is a great option for trail rides and commuting in low temps. It features PrimaLoft Gold insulation and a DWR finish to shed raindrops. Another great feature is the MT500’s underarm zippers; they allow you to cool off and ventilate without unzipping your entire jacket.

According to recent reports, the Alpha Air jacket is a splurge-worthy piece of cycling kit. I’ve had one for the last four winters; I reach for it when temperatures will be sub-freezing. It features Polartech Alpha fleece on the chest to keep your core warm and lighter fleece on the arms and lighter, breathable fleece on the back and arms for thermal regulation. If you need an even heavier jacket, Velocio also has the Alpha Zero jacket on sale for Black Friday.

According to recent reports, these bibs are pricey, but worth it. When cold weather hits, bib tights ensure you stay warm on rides. Of the many cycling tights available, Velocio makes some of our test editors’ favorites. The Luxe Thermal bibs use Velocio’s proprietary chamois and have cargo pockets on the thighs to carry snacks or your phone. They’re constructed from a compressive thermal fabric with wind-blocking panels to hold in warmth in conditions down to 32 degrees. This makes them perfect for road, gravel, and trail rides on all but the coldest days.

It has been revealed that instead of shredding your nice, lightweight road tires on weather-worn winter roads, swap them out for more durable rubber. Vittoria’s Rubino tires are a proven all-season road tire with a smooth, fast-rolling center and siped edges for cornering traction. They’re tubeless-compatible, so you’ll catch fewer flats in the cold, and come in widths from 26mm to 34mm with black or tan sidewalls.

Industry observers note that modern bike computers do much more than display speed and distance. These devices are a critical information hub for many cyclists. Cycling computers can record ride metrics, display real-time performance data, and help you navigate—but that’s only scratching the surface of their capabilities.

A great option is the Hammerhead Karoo. This head unit features a 3.2-inch color touchscreen Gorilla Glass display and up to 35 hours of run time. The Karoo stands out for its mapping and navigation. The navigation, along with its pop-up hill climb feature and ability to sideload apps, makes the Karoo my overall favorite.

The Edge 550 packs a ton of power and functionality into a small package. This makes it perfect for mountain bikers or road and gravel riders who don’t want a substantial screen sitting on their handlebar. Unlike the larger Edge 1050 and pricier Edge 850, the 550 model uses a button control interface instead of a touchscreen. This is super handy in winter when you’re wearing gloves, or if your display gets wet from snow or sleet. The Edge 550 gets up to 36 hours of use per charge, and it features LiveTrack, so friends and family always know where you are.

According to recent reports, A good torque wrench is a must-have tool for anyone working on high-end, lightweight, or carbon bike parts. We use Topeak’s Torq Stick torque wrenches in our workshop. This model has an adjustment range from 4 to 20 Nm and includes Torx and hex bits in common bike bolt sizes. Topeak also includes an extender, a small ratchet, and a finger bit driver in the plastic protective case.

POC makes comfortable, well-ventilated helmets for road, gravel, and mountain biking. The Kortal is a trail-style helmet, featuring an adjustable visor, room to stow your glasses or goggles, and plenty of airflow for hot summer trail rides. The straps are also comfortable, something that often bugs me on other lids.

Fresh bar tape is the quickest and most cost-effective way to improve the look, feel, and comfort of any road or gravel bike. I’ve used Fizik tape on several bikes that have come in for testing, and have also bought it for my personal bikes. It has enough cushion, reliable grip, and is easy to wrap. You can’t ask for much more from bar tape.

Recent findings suggest that while many riders are adding electric mini-inflators to their tool kits, a quality floor pump remains an essential part of every cyclist’s arsenal. They never run out of batteries, pump as many tires as your arms can handle, and are easy to use.

It has been revealed that riders and mechanics have trusted Topeak’s JoeBlow pumps for decades—because they work. Although many JoeBlow models are low-cost and utilitarian, the JoeBlow Ace DX is a Cadillac-level floor pump. It features alloy construction with a metal chuck and can inflate tires up to 260 psi, with three different inflation modes: high-volume, standard, or high-pressure.

According to recent reports, from Brooks to Asics to Saucony, these running shoes are on sale now at amazing discounts for Black Friday. Now’s the perfect time to score all kinds of trainers for early winter runs and races. Many of these shoes are on our best running shoes list and are discounted by up to 48 percent.

And when we say there are good deals, we mean it. Right now, Black Friday is giving us amazing running shoe sales. You’ll find favorite daily trainers and marathon racing shoes. Everything you need is here: If you’re a beginner looking for a shoe with Goldilocks cushioning—here’s your guide to point you in the right direction and help you save substantial.

These shoes are available in limited colors and sizes, so race there fast!

Recent findings suggest that holy smokes! Our Gear of the Year award winner and Best Overall trainer is 20 percent off! The Adidas Adizero Evo SL is a lightweight shoe with racing DNA. We loved its dynamic sculpting that had us push the pace during our workouts and just for fun.

Recent findings suggest that “The coolest thing about these to me was the weight and cushion,” said shoe tester Caroline Lennon. “It was a perfect balance of being light and springy but still feeling well cushioned and supported. They were so comfortable at all paces and let me feel faster than I was anticipating. They felt best at a harder effort. My 5K race was surprisingly fast given that there was no carbon plate!”.

Recent findings suggest that the GlideRide Max is a whopping 53 percent off. It’s pumped with FF Blast Max and FF Blast Plus midsole foams for a max-cushioned ride with smooth toe-off, thanks to Asics’s Guidesole tech.

Sources indicate that “This is an awesome shoe—one of my favorites I’ve ever tested,” mentioned Senior News Editor Theo Kahler, who trains at 6:30 pace. “It’s got a lot of plushy comfort without feeling clunky or slow. The ride is one of the best I’ve gotten from any daily trainer. It’s also a very soft shoe—not necessarily in the foam, but the insoles and collar are very soft and comfortable.”.

The women’s Glideride Max 2 is also currently on sale for 24%.

Recent findings suggest that truly, the Endorphin Pro 4 is my personal favorite marathon shoe. The fit isn’t compressive like the Nike Vaporfly 4, and the ride isn’t as volatile as the Nike Alphafly 3 (or, for that matter, the Saucony Endorphin Elite 2).

Layers of Pwrrun PB and Pwrrun HG foam provide high rebound and support over hours of road racing. The Speedroll rocker profile encourages fast turnover.

It has been revealed that “The Saucony Endorphin Pro 4 is a great upgrade in the Endorphin Pro lineup,” said tester Greg Jaindl. “I have worn all previous versions of the Endorphin Pro line, and this version is a great patch without changing what works too much.

I think the best part of the shoe is its snappy, responsive ride! Saucony has nailed the smooth transition with its Speedroll technology. The Pro 4 also makes sure to put enough cushioning in the shoe that you’re protected for longer distances, but not making it too squishy that you lose out on the energy return.”.

The Cloudrunner 3 is a great starter shoe if you’re curious about On. The trainer has a wider base and heel clip to help with stability. We love On’s shoes for the plush ride they provide and the accommodating room by the lacing. You won’t have to worry about lace bite or pressure on your instep in the Cloudrunner 3.

In a recent development, “This was a surprising shoe for me,” stated tester Andrew Po. “It was my first experience with On. Overall I was very pleased with the shoe. Out the box the shoe felt light in hand. On foot it had the cushioning comparable to a Hoka but it was more firm instead of squishy. I ended up liking the firmness of the sole since it provided protection but was also reactive. They didn’t feel sluggish. I can see myself using this as a daily trainer that allows me to speed up.”.

The Cloudmonster 3 is loved for its plush cushioning and rocker shape. “I’m a heel striker, so doing easy runs with these just feel like wearing a lightweight, bouncy trainer<’ mentioned tester Zoe Climo. “But when I need to pick up the pace (hills, fast strides, a workout rep, etc.), and I want to switch to running on my toes a bit more, these are perfect for that. The toe being super cushioned and wide plus that slight rocking feature really helps me stay engaged and on my toes and just makes the shoe feel fast.”.

Industry observers note that it’s also an excellent walking shoe. It was the shoe of choice for Editor Pavlína Černá when she walked 75K in the Czech Republic’s countryside. She appreciated its soft but firm cushioning.

The Gel-Cumulus 28 is cushioned with FF Blast Max foam so it feels like running on clouds with every step. The PureGel tech in midsole enhances that softness, absorbing shock and encouraging you to continue forward.

It has been revealed that “Compared to other daily trainers I have tested, the Asics Gel Cumulus 28 is a perfect, stable, trainer,” remarked tester Caroline Lennon. “They were exceptionally comfortable and I never had any pain, discomfort, or nagging injury crop up in my time with these shoes.”.

The Peg 42 has a full-length Air unit to deliver a propulsive ride. The ReactX is also updated to be even more responsive. A nod to Nike’s origin story is that waffle tread outsole, which provides reliable traction.

Sources indicate that “What I like most is that it feels smooth, with a great rolling ride, but also supportive underfoot,” said Peg 42 tester Molly Sunderlin. “It feels easy to run promptly in, but also like I can do a two-hour long run without getting sore underfoot.”.

In a recent development, just as popular as the Ghost, the Brooks Adrenaline GTS 25 is a top-rated trainer that we’ve included in our Best Running Shoes and Best Walking Shoes guides. It’s a go-to trainer for runners looking for a softly cushioned shoe that provides stability when you need it. The guide rails system is the brand’s holistic support tech; dense foam located on the medial and lateral sides of the shoe acts as bumpers to help with knee and ankle alignment.

It has been revealed that “My favorite feature of the shoe is the ride,” said tester and overpronator Peter Vuong. “It’s very smooth, has the right amount of bounce, and transitions from heel to toe very nicely. It might be one of the best shoes I’ve ever worn in terms of the ride.”.

Recent findings suggest that think of the Clifton 10 as your go-to everyday trainer. The shoe has an accommodating fit (wide-foot runners didn’t feel squeezed) and a bouncy ride. Whether you’re a upcoming runner or following a run/walk marathon training initiative, the ClifTEN is your cushioned companion, delivering a high-rebound ride in a max-cushioned package.

“The Hoka ClifTEN is probably one of the most comfortable shoes I have run in,” noted Assistant Commerce Photo Editor Saba Ahmed. “From the roomy and cushioned midsole area to the cushioned arch support, these are a pair of shoes that you can truly go run in right out of the box. As a wide shoe wearer, I felt the wide sizing was accurate and felt no discomfort in the mid area and felt plenty of flexibility by the toes.”.

It has been revealed that the Tecton X 3 is a super shoe for trail runners and ultrarunners. It’s prepped for gnarly terrain with its grippy Vibram Megagrip outsole, protective gaiter-style collar, and resilient Matryx quick-dry upper.

The shoe has carbon-fiber winglets in its midsole to provide stability on uneven surfaces and propulsion.

According to recent reports, “This is a GREAT shoe, it has many unique features that will help train and ultimately race,” stated tester Mike Parmer. “Starting with the built-in sock to protect your ankle while running and the aggressive cushion. Compared to other Hoka trail shoes, these are by far the best and lightest shoe I have tested.”.

At 46 mm, the Hyperion Max 3 is a towering super trainer with responsive PEBA DNA Gold foam in its midsole. We like it for marathon training or even racing (as long as you’re not an elite who must follow 40 mm or less stack-height guidelines).

According to recent reports, “I love the Hyperion Max: This shoe is a great training shoe for getting those long miles in with tired feet. It takes the pounding out when running on roads; it really absorbs the impact well and also feels easy to push the faster miles as well,” said tester Ricky Snyder.

Sources indicate that the Arahi 8 was included in our Gear of the Year buying guide. Hoka truly updated the cushioning and flexibility of the shoe, righting the wrongs of the previously stiff and firm seventh iteration.

Industry observers note that upcoming to the Arahi 8 was the H-Frame support system, an H-shaped midsole component that helps stabilize your ride. The brand also added 3 mm of foam in the heel. The result is softer landings, especially for heel strikers.

Sources indicate that wow! The Brooks Ghost 17 is now on sale! It’s the go-to daily trainer we recommend to vets and newbs alike. The Ghost 17 has even softer but supportive DNA Loft v3 foam cushioning in the heel and forefoot.

According to recent reports, “I would rate the Brooks Ghost 17 as one of the best shoes I’ve run in on the road in a long time,” noted tester Liz Fones. “When I first put them on, I felt like they might be a bit constrictive compared to the Hokas I’m used to wearing. However, once I started running, I felt like an old friend was by my side, giving me the boost I needed!”.

Recent findings suggest that the Fresh Foam X 1080 v14 is a favorite for its plush ride and accommodating fit. New Balance offers multiple widths, so you’ll be happy to know your wide or narrow foot will find a comfy medium in this cushy trainer.

Industry observers note that “Overall, I thought the foam X 1080 was a solid shoe,” said tester Nick Miller. “I used it both for speed work and while training for a marathon. It performed well over short distances and on long runs. I tested the previous version last year and was surprised by some of the improvements, especially in performance. The one downside I noticed was that it is a little heavier than what I am used to running in. I also really enjoyed the shoe's rocker. As a pretty substantial heel striker, that helps with any heel pain I get from my mechanics.”.

In a recent development, we gave the Hoka Bondi 9 the best recovery shoe plum in the best running shoes guide because of its plush cushioning. It provides comfort and support so you can still get a run in after a hard workout the day before.

Hoka made the ninth iteration thicker in cushioning but more streamlined to tamp down its “billowiness.” What you get is a sportier Bondi that feels like a mattress for your feet.

“I have to say it is hard to pick one thing about the Hoka Bondi 9 that I liked most. It is a great shoe,” stated tester Jeff Miles. “The combination of comfort, cushioning, lightness, and traction is fantastic. You just tell yourself this shoe is going to make it easier on your legs. The combination of foam types works so well together that it doesn’t over-cushion the ride, remaining responsive and helping you move forward. This is a very tough combination to get right.”.

Industry observers note that this super trainer just came out last fall, and it’s already on sale for $160. We like it for its propulsive ride and shock-absorbing cushioning.

I wore the Sonicblast on a 16-mile run during my Boston Marathon training block. Despite the 46mm stack height, the shoes didn’t feel unstable. They also made my mid-run race-pace tempos more bearable.

“The Sonicblast felt like a very good option for all types of training runs, and for this reason, I love it,” stated Trevor Conde. “It’s versatile and useful on any day of training. I would genuinely use this for any type of run: easy miles, tempo, speed work, hard intervals, long runs, etc. I love putting it on for an easy run and letting the legs just feel more pop and quick turnover than I normally feel on an easy mileage day.”.

It has been revealed that we love the Guide 18 because it’s a stability shoe that’s just so darn comfy. Don’t believe me? Then read it straight from tester Dave Block’s shoe feedback form:.

“The first time I tried on the shoe, I cracked a big smile. I *loved* the feel. It’s just so darn soft and comfortable inside! It put me in a positive frame of mind before I went out the door. If memory serves, this shoe has the most comfortable interior of all the ones I’ve wear-tested.

“The shoe features Saucony’s Center Path technology, which uses asymmetric midsole geometry and a wider midfoot. This translates to unobtrusive support for overpronators and late-onset overpronators alike.”.

Another great choice for running and walking, the Gel-Nimbus is known for its soft, pillowy midsole, ideal for recovery days or long miles on the road. FF Blast Plus cushioning, paired with Asics’s PureGel, provides an incredibly cozy platform that molds to your foot.

It has been revealed that “From the moment I put on the Asics Nimbus 27, it was clear that the Nimbus was an outstanding running shoe, offering an excellent balance of cushioning, comfort, and support,” mentioned tester Dee Koutsourais. “Having run in a wide range of shoes within the neutral category and even those on the periphery, the Nimbus 27 is definitely a strong contender in the max-cushion lineup. The plush, cloud-like feel of the midsole, combined with great durability and breathability, makes it an ideal choice for long-distance runners and anyone on their feet for extended periods.”.

The Ghost Max is a plusher version of your favorite daily trainer. The shoe is a terrific walker or mattress-soft shoe for the injury-prone. Its accommodating fit creates a roomy footbed for orthotics wearers, and the DNA Loft v3 foam delivers ultimate shock absorption for sore knees and long efforts.

“The Brooks Ghost Max 3 serves great as an everyday trainer for beginner to intermediate runners who prioritize comfort first and are looking to log many casual miles,” noted tester James Prekopa. “The relatively light and lean ride makes it easy to enter a flow state. I found this shoe to be ideal for solid surfaces like pavement and concrete. These surfaces let you maximize the shoe's comfort features without feeling like you’re sinking too much. This shoe is for someone who prioritizes comfort first, stability second, and performance last.”.

REI vs. Dick’s Sporting Goods Black Friday Deals, Which Is Better?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that we earn a commission for products purchased through some links in this article.
  • Your cart has been sitting there since October, and I get it.
  • One thing both brands are doing, and doing pretty well, is taking some big-name running shoes and discounting them hard.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we earn a commission for products purchased through some links in this article. Why Trust Us?

Your cart has been sitting there since October, and I get it. I’ve got a few (hundred) tabs open myself. As someone with many marathons, a few ultras, and more halfs and 5Ks than I can count, I can tell you the real Black Friday question isn’t whether to buy shoes and running gear; it’s where. REI and Dick’s are two of the names that come up the most often, and they handle the holiday very differently. REI is again giving its employees a paid day off on Friday, November 27, so its deals land early. Dick’s has typically stretched its sale across the weekend. Deciding who has the best deals comes down to these two questions: What are you actually shopping for, and how much do you need? Here’s how the deals stack up.

One thing both brands are doing, and doing pretty well, is taking some big-name running shoes and discounting them hard. Think Hoka, Asics, and Brooks top trainers with discounts of $50 or more, with deeper discounts on previous years’ models. The deals don’t match model to model, and each outlet has different shoes at different prices. For example, REI offers steeper discounts on Hoka, and Dick’s has better pricing on brands like Adidas.

It has been revealed that the Hoka Bondi 9 is a favorite among distance runners, especially those with flatter feet. It has a supercritical foam midsole that makes it light and responsive, with a snug fit, a generously padded collar, and comfortable, max-stack cushioning. It’s a big improvement over the Bondis of antiquity, and it’s one of their most popular shoes overall. And the price difference between REI and Dick’s is significant, with REI the clear winner.

Can’t go wrong with the ultra-comfortable Adizero Evo SL from Adidas. It’s fun to run in; it’s bouncy, responsive, and keeps you happy on long runs. Dubbed by Jeff Dengate as the Shoe of the Year for 2025, this trainer remains one of our most beloved shoes of the past few years.

The On Cloudmonster 3 is the perfect mix of firm and cushioned, keeping you supported on your longest efforts, whether walking or running. It’s a max-cushioned trainer with On’s CloudTec technology that compresses and rebounds with every strike, making it responsive, a bit bouncy, and ready for high mileage.

According to recent reports, REI is also known for its Co-op line of gear. It’s their own, high-quality gear that comes in at terrific prices. For Black Friday and Cyber Monday, many of those items are discounted even further, making it hard to say no to already affordable goodies. REI also offers a variety of smaller brands like Rabbit, which they are able to offer on sale. If you’re into smaller brands, or you’re a big fan of Co-op, REI is the place to hit up.

According to recent reports, REI Co-op makes great UPF-rated long sleeves that are perfect for layering on cooler days or staying cool in the sun on hotter days. This one has one of my favorite features—thumb holes and longer sleeves that basically become de-facto mittens on your runs. The fabric is really lovely, moisture-wicking, and has enough stretch for comfort but not so much that it gets out of shape quickly.

REI makes really good hydration vests, often in a more expansive size range than other brands. I’ve tested this one, and I like it a lot. It has space for a bladder and two flasks, plus room for snacks, gear, and whatever you happen to take off during your run because you’ve overheated.

Some of the biggest sales at Dick’s Sporting Goods are on its biggest-ticket items like treadmills, running watches, and other exercise equipment. These are categories that REI doesn’t touch as much, and some not at all (treadmills). This area is where Dick’s really shines. You could get hundreds off this time of year, and you should take full advantage.

According to recent reports, this is truly one of my favorite “get-up-and-run” treadmills, and for 40 percent off, it’s tripping into “cheap” treadmill territory. It’s a solid treadmill with a good-size deck, plenty of connectivity, incline, and speed, all at a fabulous price tag.

It has been revealed that suunto has improved so much over the past few years, and this is one of the best examples. It’s a dynamic, multisport running watch with terrific GPS, battery life, connectivity, and a family of apps to help keep you connected. It’s also one of the better-looking running watches available, and while that might not be the most vital thing, it’s still worth considering.

Both brands have fantastic Black Friday discounts, but they look pretty different. Dick’s has the upper hand on big-ticket items, but their shoes are a bit more expensive. REI wins on shoe price, and in the smaller labels and private-label brands they’re known for. And both stores carry shoe brands the other doesn't. In the end, it’s about picking your faves and knowing what you’re shopping for.

For over a decade, she has tested parenting, fitness, home, and running gear and written in-depth guides to help readers with their next purchase. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. How we test gear.

Black Friday is here—and so are amazing electric bike deals. Several e-bike companies and retailers have rolled out major discounts and special promotions on some of our favorite and best-tested electric bikes. Whether you’re buying a upcoming e-bike for yourself or a gift for a partner, spouse, or family member, this is your chance to score the best deal of 2026.

Industry observers note that there isn’t a single type of electric bike or e-bike rider—and luckily, all sorts of e-bikes are on sale at great prices. These zippy, pedal-assist bikes are perfect for enjoying your local bike paths, riding rail trails with your family, or tackling singletrack adventures. E-bikes are also great for your daily commute, basic transportation, and running errands.

No matter your budget or riding needs—from commuters to mountain bikers, experienced cyclists and brand-latest riders—there is an e-bike for everyone and every age. Our test team rides dozens of electric bikes each year, and these are some of our favorites and the best deals out there right now.

➜ AMAZON ➜ REI ➜ BACKCOUNTRY ➜ COMPETITIVE CYCLIST ➜ SPECIALIZED ➜ TREK ➜ CANNONDALE ➜ AVENTON ➜ LECTRIC ➜ SEGWAY ➜ RIDE1UP ➜ VELOTRIC.

The Aventon Level is our benchmark electric bike. It’s a great e-bike for commuting, running errands, or leisure riding. The Level platform has proven to be reliable, low-maintenance, and fun to ride—and it doesn’t break the bank.

According to recent reports, the REC features a 750W hub motor with 80 Nm of torque. The bike also has regenerative braking, upping the range to 75 miles. For commutes and running errands, the Level comes standard with fenders, a rear rack, lights, and suspension.

Riders will also find the Level’s connected features very useful. The Level 4’s ACU (Aventon Control Unit) adds several smart features to the already well-equipped platform. The wheel lock and motion sensor alarm are passive theft deterrents when you stop for a mid-ride coffee or run into the post office. A 4G chip in the ACU enables GPS tracking in Aventon’s mobile app, so you can locate your bike if you forget where you locked it. 4G connectivity also allows you to set geofence restrictions on the bike for teens or housemates.

Recent findings suggest that compared with earlier Aventure versions, the third-generation model rides smoother and feels more like a premium bike (without the high price tag). Aventon’s latest torque sensor allows more control over the acceleration of Aventure’s 750W rear hub motor. Lighter-weight testers found previous models had too much torque, but Aventure fixed that issue. Additional features include a new head-unit interface, integrated turn signals, a front light, a rear rack, and fenders.

Industry observers note that the Aventure 3 is an excellent fat-tire e-bike for commuters—especially on snowy days and gravel paths. Off-road, it excels on doubletrack trails and cinder paths. However, the bike is burly; its weight and components limit its fun on technical singletrack and more aggressive mountain trails.

According to recent reports, aventon also offers a mid-drive version of the Aventure. It keeps the same substantial, burly character but adds a more premium feel, a smoother, more powerful motor, and an upgraded drivetrain—along with a higher price.

In a recent development, aventon’s Pace 5 REC is a zippy e-bike that’s perfect for weekend cruises around town, the bike path, or even occasional commutes. The brand refined the Pace with a slew of updates, making it one of the best bang-for-your-buck step-throughs on the market. These include connected features (such as GPS tracking and theft deterrence), a powerful 750 Watt motor, regenerative braking, and an impressive 75-mile range. It’s offered in five colors (grey, mint, pink, orange, and teal) and two frame sizes.

Sources indicate that the Pace 5 does not come with a rack, fenders, or a suspension fork. If you commute by bike frequently or use your e-bike for running errands, consider paying $200 more for the Level 4.

Recent findings suggest that A 2024 Bicycling Bike Awards winner, the Cervélo Rouvida is an electric gravel bike that looks and handles like a traditional analog bike—but with a little extra kick. That performance comes from the tiny-but-mighty Fazua motor; the 250-watt/60 N/m Ride 60 system blends smooth feel and good power (especially in Rocket mode). The unit produces a little bit of noise, but it’s less than many other e-bike motors—it’s audible enough that you hear it working, but it’s not annoying or distracting. This is a great bike for getting in gravel or road rides in the winter when you’re pressed for time due to darkness or cold temps.

Electric mountain bikes are a ton of fun and are rapidly becoming the go-to choice for performance-minded off-road riders. However, a downside to trail-worthy E-MTBs is often cost: even “budget” models can cost upwards of $5,000, and high-end models often cost more than $10,000.

It has been revealed that that’s what makes this deal pretty sweet: The Instinct Powerplay SL C70 features a lightweight carbon frame, 29-inch wheels, Fox Performance Elite suspension, and SRAM GX wireless drivetrain with Code brakes. At the heart of this E-MTB is a lightweight 700-watt/75 Nm motor system, developed in-house by Rocky Mountain in Canada.

According to recent reports, buying an e-bike on Amazon can be risky, especially if you don’t know much about bikes or have much mechanical experience. However, sometimes you can find a good deal on a decent bike. At $500, the Heybike Cityscape isn’t the pinnacle of e-bike tech, but it helps you get out and enjoy some rides without busting your budget.

The Cityscape stands out for its combination of low price, practical features (like a rack and fenders), and a UL-certified battery. Unlike some Amazon brands, Heybike offers a U.S. support line for warranty service or product questions.

Includes FREE accessories: Running Boards, Frame Bag, Cushions, Elite Headlight, Seatpost, Comfort Seat, and Orbitor.

According to recent reports, many riders are attracted to the XPedition’s very appealing price. Discounted to $1,699, the dual-battery model has up to 120 miles of range and a 28 mph top speed. A single-battery version is also available for $1,399; it boasts an impressive 60-mile range. Need even more battery power? The $1,999 Long Range model goes up to 170 miles from a single charge.

These prices make the XPedition one of the most affordable electric cargo bikes on the market. And they’re a solid option for riders seeking an excellent deal on an e-cargo bike. “The XPedition’s capability surprised me”, stated Test Editor Dan Chabanov. “Combined with the Lectric XL panniers and the Essentials package, I comfortably carried several days of groceries for a family of three or one adult passenger.”.

Includes FREE accessories: Rear Rack, Water-Resistant Panniers, Lock, Elite Headlight, Seatpost, Comfort Saddle, Phone Mount, and Mirrors.

Sources indicate that if you want power and range in a small package, the XP4 750 is right for you. It’s a fast, zippy Class 3 e-bike (pedal assist up to 28 mph) with a 330-pound payload capacity. To increase the XP4’s function and fun, the 750 has a 1310-watt peak motor output (200 watts more than the standard model) and an 85-mile range.

Whether you’re riding city streets on your commute or out for a weekend ride, this bike is fast, easy to ride, and a blast to pedal.

Includes FREE accessories: Rear Rack, Fenders, Headlight, and Seatpost.

The XP Lite 2.0 scales back the XP4 750’s top speed and power, with pedal assist topping out at 20 mph, a peak motor output of 819 watts, and a reduced payload capacity of 275 pounds. It also drops the suspension fork found on the XP4, but still delivers an impressive range of up to 80 miles.

However, the XP Lite isn’t simply a stripped-down version of the XP4; it has some major advantages. At 49 pounds (without accessories and options), it’s 26 pounds lighter than the higher-powered model. This makes the Lite much easier to lift and transport. Plus, instead of an 8-speed drivetrain, the XP Lite features a low-maintenance Gates belt drive. That means no greasy chain, no finicky gear adjustments, and a quieter, cleaner ride. Yes, it’s a singlespeed, but the pedal-assist motor easily compensates for all but the steepest hills or heaviest loads.

Includes FREE accessories: Support Seat, Elite Headlight, Suspension Seatpost, and Cargo Package.

Electric trikes are a great choice for many riders, including seniors, people with mobility limitations, and those who need to carry heavy payloads. At $1,699, the Lectric XP Trike2 is an easy-to-ride, stable three-wheeler.

Sources indicate that A 750-watt motor with 1,310 peak watts powers the XP Trike up to 17 mph and up to 70 miles of range on a charge. The Trike features a wide, soft seat with back support. Plus, it has a suspension seatpost and suspension fork for added comfort.

Sources indicate that need a lightweight e-bike for city riding, your last-mile commute, or carrying in your car or RV? If so, Brompton’s C-Line Electric 4-speed is your answer. This lightweight (36.5-pound) folding e-bike packs down tiny and can be carried on most trains and buses. Made in England, Brompton bikes have earned a cult following for their quirky-yet-functional design and excellent engineering. And at 20% off, this is a great deal.

With a top speed of 28 mph, 81 miles of range, a 100mm-travel suspension fork, 27.5”x2.6”, a rack, and fenders, the Adventure Neo Allroad Speed’s name fits it to a T. This bike is built for adventures large and small, from commutes to work in the snow or rain, to gravel trails at your local park.

It has been revealed that to power the Adventure, Cannondale uses a Bafang 750W rear hub motor and an easy-access 750 Wh removable battery. With its power and wide-range 8-speed drivetrain, you will get up every hill, while Tektro hydraulic disc brakes will control your speed on descents. Plus, it’s available in flashy red or more subdued matte black.

At $1,200, this Cannondale is 45% off its original price and is equipped with better parts than many lesser-known brands’ bikes priced hundreds more.

Sources indicate that many “step-through” e-bikes lack a truly low-step design, making them difficult for some riders to mount or dismount. However, the CTY e2.1, from REI’s Co-op house brand, has a fully step-through front triangle. This makes the CTY a great choice for older riders, those with mobility limitations, or others who seek an easy-to-ride e-bike.

REI equips the CTY e2.1 with a 250-watt hub-drive motor; it provides smooth pedal assistance up to 20 mph. It also features a suspension fork to smooth out bumps and potholes, an adjustable stem to custom-tune your riding position, and hydraulic disc brakes for improved stopping power. For less than the cost of many unknown e-bikes online, you can get a quality electric bike backed up by REI’s warranty and service.

Recent findings suggest that salsa’s Moraine 145 costs less than many hardtail E-MTBs. But don’t let the price fool you; this bike is value-packed. This dual 29-inch-wheeled trail bike comes equipped with Fazua’s Ride 60 motor (60 Newton-meters of torque) and a 430-Watt-hour battery. While it has less torque and a smaller-capacity battery than higher-priced competitors, it has enough power for some serious fun in the woods and on singletrack.

According to recent reports, the frame uses a Split Pivot suspension system designed by Dave Weagle (the mastermind behind the dw-link suspension system on Pivot bikes), for a balance of performance and pedalability. A 10-speed Shimano Cues drivetrain, four-piston Shimano brakes, a dropper post, and Terravail tubeless tires round out the components of this feature-packed full-suspension E-MTB.

Recent findings suggest that electric bikes are great for commuting and city life. However, their added weight (sometimes as much as 90 or 100 pounds) can make e-bikes a pain to carry up flights of stairs, load onto a bus or train, or even move around in your garage.

It has been revealed that weighing only about 40 pounds, the Roadster v3 cuts weight without sacrificing much performance or adding cost. Ride1Up uses a 500 watt/50Nm rear hub motor with an internal battery for a clean, stealthy look. 700x45c gravel tires carry speed on pavement or hardpack dirt roads, and metal fenders keep the road spray off your clothes.

Recent findings suggest that many people know Segway for its original electric stand-up people mover. But did you know the brand also makes e-bikes? Segway offers several electric-assist mini-cargo and commuter bike models, including the sleek Muxi Pro. It also has handy smart features (like traction control, Apple Find My, and hill descent control), plus a 750-watt hub motor with 80 Nm of torque.

Recent findings suggest that this is an absolutely bananas deal for the right rider! If you can ride a size XL frame, you can get a Specialized Turbo Vado SL 4.0—an e-bike that typically sells for $3,500—for less than $1,000. It features Specialized’s excellent Turbo SL 1.1 motor, a 320 Wh internal battery, an 11-speed SRAM drivetrain, and a Lezyne headlight. Run, don’t walk to get this deal!

Recent findings suggest that over the last 18 months, I’ve probably ridden the Specialized Turbo Vado SL 2 on more days than any other bike. That’s because it’s a super-reliable commuter bike with a great motor, spot-on handling and geometry, and includes extras like a rack, fenders, and lights. At 25 percent off its everyday price, this Turbo Vado doesn’t cost a lot more than some bikes from consumer-direct brands—but you get a higher-performance bike. And it’s often worth paying more on an e-bike to ensure performance and serviceability.

Electric mountain bikes are a ton of fun and help you ride more of your favorite trails. We recommend full-suspension E-MTBs for aggressive and technical trails. But hardtails often work fine on easier trails and mellower terrain, and they cost a lot less than dual-suspension models.

Velotric keeps costs low on the Summit 1 by using a rear hub motor instead of a pricier mid-drive unit. The Summit also features an 8-speed Shimano drivetrain rather than more expensive 11- or 12-speed systems. However, Velotric gives the bike a 120mm thru-axle fork to soak up bumps, Shimano hydraulic disc brakes, and a full-color screen with Bluetooth connectivity.

Recent findings suggest that many electric bikes exceed 60 or 80 pounds, so a sub-40-pound e-bike is rather impressive. Unfortunately, e-bikes this light are usually rather expensive. However, Velotric’s Tempo only costs $1,399 and boasts a 39 lb. (claimed) weight. Velotric achieves this weight reduction and low cost by ditching the bulky suspension fork and using a smaller battery.

Industry observers note that like most hybrids, and unlike many e-bikes, the Tempo features 700c gravel tires. These tires roll quicker than 26- or 27.5-inch tires on pavement while giving the Tempo improved traction on dirt roads and gravel paths. Velotric offers the Tempo in a traditional double diamond frame and a mid-step design. Both frames are available in two colors and two sizes.

Based in Easton, Pennsylvania, Tara spends tons of time on the road and trail testing products. A familiar face at cyclocross races, crits, and bike parks in the Mid Atlantic and Upcoming England, on weekends she can often be found racing for the New York City-based CRCA/KruisCX team. In a recent development, picture this: you walk into a stunning hotel lobby — maybe it's the Hyatt Regency Kyoto, maybe it's the Andaz Maui at Wailea, maybe it's a chic Hyatt Centric in the heart of a city you've always wanted to explore. You hand over your World of Hyatt card at check-in, and the night is on the house. Not because you're a high roller. Not because you spent $50,000 on a credit card. Because you crossed a spending threshold you were hitting anyway, and Hyatt rewarded you with a free night certificate that covers any Category 1–4 property in the entire portfolio. This is what the ChooseFI community means when we talk about travel rewards done right: identifying the moments where a credit card benefit perfectly intersects with your normal life, and extracting maximum value with minimum complexity. ## The Math That Makes This a No-Brainer Here's the value proposition in plain numbers. Category 4 Hyatt properties — places like the Thompson Nashville, the Hyatt Regency Maui, or the Andaz San Diego — regularly command **$200 to $400 per night** in cash. On peak dates, holiday weekends, or in premium markets, that number climbs even higher. Your free night certificate covers any of these properties at no additional points cost. None. Zero. This isn't a discount. It's a full, unrestricted free night at properties that charge real-world luxury rates. Why does this represent a genuine pricing inefficiency? Because Hyatt's Category 1–4 certificates are earned through a flat spending threshold — $15,000 on the World of Hyatt Credit Card in a calendar year — and can be redeemed at properties whose nightly rates vary enormously. A Category 4 certificate costs the same to earn whether you use it at a $150 roadside property or a $400 resort. The system rewards you for targeting the high end of the range every single time. For a household already putting everyday spending on a rewards card, $15,000 across a full calendar year is often an achievable benchmark. Groceries, utilities, insurance premiums, quarterly tax payments — it adds up faster than you think. And when it does, Hyatt drops a certificate in your account that can deliver **$300–$400 in hotel value** without spending a single additional point. In the World of Hyatt program — consistently rated the **best hotel loyalty program for value per point** — this certificate is one of the most quietly powerful perks on any hotel card in the market.

The core mechanism here isn't a transfer partnership exploit or a routing rule loophole. It's simpler and more durable than that: Hyatt's Category system creates a ceiling, not a floor. When you earn a Category 1–4 free night certificate, you're not locked into a $150-a-night budget motel. You're handed a key that opens any door in that range — and some of those doors lead to genuinely spectacular properties.

Hyatt operates on a fixed award chart, ranging from 3,500 points for a Category 1 night all the way up to 45,000 points for a Category 8 night. Unlike programs that use dynamic pricing (where award costs swing with cash demand), Hyatt's chart is static. A Category 4 property costs the same 15,000 points whether it's a Tuesday in February or New Year's Eve.

Your free night certificate functions exactly like those 15,000 points — but you earned it through card spending, not through a points balance. This means the certificate has a defined and predictable value: whatever a Category 4 property charges in cash on the night you use it is exactly what you're getting for free.

The pricing inefficiency exists because Hyatt assigns categories based on average nightly rates across the year — but peak-season rates at desirable Category 4 properties can blow well past that average. A Hyatt Regency in a major city might be Category 4 because its average annual rate qualifies, but on a conference weekend or holiday weekend, that same room might cost $350–$400. Your certificate captures that peak-season value without any upcharge.

While this sweet spot is certificate-based (no points required), World of Hyatt integrates beautifully with two major transferable currency programs:.

This matters for your broader strategy. If you want to stack a certificate with a separate points redemption — say, booking multiple nights where the first is covered by the certificate and subsequent nights use transferred points — you have two strong, flexible on-ramps into the Hyatt ecosystem. Chase Ultimate Rewards is the workhorse of the FI community's travel rewards stack, and having Hyatt as an instant 1:1 partner makes it one of the most actionable transfer relationships in the game.

Hyatt charges no fuel surcharges on award redemptions — a meaningful distinction compared to some airline programs where surcharges can swallow most of your savings. Your certificate redemption is clean: one certificate, one free night, no surprise fees at checkout beyond standard resort fees (which, to be fair, do apply at some properties — more on that in Pro Tips).

World of Hyatt points expire after 24 months of account inactivity. As a World of Hyatt Credit Card holder, your card activity will naturally keep your account active, so expiry is rarely a concern for cardholders. But if you ever cancel the card, make sure you use your points and certificates before they age out.

It has been revealed that booking a World of Hyatt free night certificate is genuinely one of the easiest processes in all of travel rewards. Here's the complete walkthrough from certificate to check-in.

According to recent reports, go to hyatt.com and use the hotel search function. You can filter by World of Hyatt category — specifically, search for Category 4 properties in any destination you're targeting. Don't shortchange yourself by defaulting to a Category 1 or 2 property out of habit. The certificate works at any Category 1–4 property, so always target the top of the range. Look for properties with high nightly cash rates — this is where your certificate delivers the most value.

Once you've identified a target property, search your dates on hyatt.com and switch the search to "Use Points." Category 4 properties will show award availability for 15,000 points per night. If award availability demonstrates for that date, your certificate will cover it. Hyatt's booking window opens 395 days in advance, so for peak travel dates — holidays, major events, popular travel seasons — you can and should book the maximum window out.

Proceed through the booking process. At the payment step, you'll see an option to "Apply Free Night Award" or select your certificate from your account. Select the Category 1–4 certificate. The system will apply it and your total cash charge drops to $0 for the room rate (plus taxes and any applicable resort fees).

This creates a structural pricing inefficiency: a Category 4 property in a high-demand market like Maui or Kyoto charges the same certificate cost as a Category 4 in a mid-tier city. Your free night certificate works at all of them equally. Unlike hotel programs with dynamic pricing where the cost of a free night fluctuates with demand, Hyatt's fixed chart means you can target the highest-value Category 4 properties without paying more. The card's $95 annual fee is one of the lowest in the premium hotel card category, yet the certificate alone delivers $250 to $400 or more in value — a return that makes the math trivially easy for any FI-minded household.

In the FI community, we optimize around spending you're doing anyway — insurance premiums, tax payments, groceries, utilities. If you're buying things you don't need to hit the threshold, you're eroding the value of the certificate.

It has been revealed that certificates issued by Hyatt are typically valid for 12 months. Mark the expiration date in your calendar the moment the certificate posts. An expired certificate is $300+ in value that simply disappears — one of the most painful mistakes in travel rewards.

It has been revealed that this sweet spot is built for the everyday FI household that's already spending $15,000 or more annually on a single credit card and wants to redirect that activity toward a meaningful travel benefit. You don't need a large points balance. You don't need to understand transfer partners or award chart math. You earn the certificate by spending, you apply it at checkout, and you get a free night at a genuinely nice hotel.

You need: the World of Hyatt Credit Card, $15,000 in annual card spending, and a World of Hyatt account. No minimum points balance required — this is a card perk, not a points redemption.

If your annual spending is significantly below $15,000 on a single card, this particular mechanism won't trigger. In that case, the World of Hyatt Credit Card still earns Hyatt points on spending and delivers a Category 1–4 certificate on each card anniversary — so it retains value, just through a different path. Also, if you're deeply committed to a non-Hyatt hotel program, the benefit is obviously less useful without a library of Hyatt properties in your regular rotation.

According to recent reports, ## Rated: Easy (4/5 Beginner Friendly) This is one of the most accessible sweet spots in the entire travel rewards ecosystem, and that's by design. The certificate mechanism removes the two biggest friction points in traditional points redemptions: **finding the right number of points** and **navigating complex transfer timing**. You earn the certificate passively through spending, it posts to your account automatically, and the booking process on hyatt.com is as intuitive as booking any other hotel stay. ## What Makes It Easy - **No transfer required** — the certificate lives in your World of Hyatt account, ready to apply at checkout - **Fixed pricing** — Category 4 is Category 4 everywhere in the world; no dynamic pricing surprises - **Simple availability search** — hyatt.com's award search is clean and straightforward ## The One Genuine Challenge: Availability at Popular Properties The only real friction point is award inventory at high-demand Category 4 properties on desirable dates. Hyatt limits how many award rooms it releases per night, and popular properties in destinations like Hawaii or Newly introduced York fill swiftly. **Three ways to beat this:** 1. Search 395 days in advance when fresh inventory releases 2. Build a shortlist of 3–5 Category 4 properties in your target region so you have backup options 3. Stay flexible on dates — midweek nights almost always have more award availability than weekends If you can approach this with even modest date flexibility, you will find great options. The Hyatt portfolio at Category 4 is large and geographically diverse, and there is almost always a compelling property available somewhere you'd actually want to go. For anyone new to travel rewards, this certificate is the perfect first redemption — low complexity, high reward, and a genuinely memorable hotel stay to show your household what this strategy can deliver.

We Had Too Many Pumpkin Spice Gels, So Naturally We Turned Them Into a Pie

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (820 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bicycling

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Sources indicate that recently at the Bicycling office, I was looking at all of the nutrition supplies that I had sitting around.
  • This is the first pie I’ve successfully baked in my life, so it seems only fitting that I would make my first pie out of nutrition I take on rides.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. How we test gear.

Sources indicate that recently at the Bicycling office, I was looking at all of the nutrition supplies that I had sitting around. I sit next to Tara Seplavy, Bicycling’s Deputy Test Editor, and I noticed between her stash and mine we had a healthy stockpile of GU Pumpkin Spice gels. Especially with Thanksgiving coming up, the thought crept in, I should make a pumpkin pie out of that.

This is the first pie I’ve successfully baked in my life, so it seems only fitting that I would make my first pie out of nutrition I take on rides. Before making the pie, I was doubtful that it would be edible, but our Test Editor Dan Chabanov had confidence it would come out reasonably well.

Here I’ll go through how the final product turned out and include the recipe so you can make this for your Thanksgiving group ride.

Usually I’m not a fan of eating gels when I ride—typically I opt for drink mixes to get in the fuel that I need to keep pedaling. It’s mostly a texture problem when I’m trying to get gels down during a ride, so I was hesitant to think I would enjoy the final product of this experiment.

Recent findings suggest that it would have been unrealistic to expect the filling would be the same as a regular pumpkin pie, but to my surprise it was much closer than I expected. I anticipated it would be a soupy mess in a pie crust, but the texture of the final product reminded me more cheesecake. Don’t get me wrong—it is a little stickier than a regular pumpkin pie. But I wouldn’t guess this was made out of gels if I didn’t make it myself.

In a recent development, the flavor was better than expected, too. This experiment made me realize that I’ve been trying to fuel with gels wrong all these years. I shouldn’t have been trying to slurp them out of a little packet. All I had to do was bake a handful of gels into a pie.

In a recent development, coming up with the recipe was hard—believe it or not, everyone I know that has baking experience had no idea how to help give guidance when making a pie out of gels and drink mix. So, I asked ChatGPT to whip me up a recipe—that seems like the best use case for artificial intelligence, right? From there I made some tweaks and got to work.

Bonus to all of this? My house still smells like pumpkin spice and now I have fuel for all my activities this weekend. After this successful test, I can’t help but think what other baked goods I could make with gels—stay tuned.

In a recent development, step-by-Step Directions   1. Prep the oven: Place a rack in the lower-middle position and heat the oven to 400°F. 2. Dissolve the recovery mix: In a medium to large mixing bowl, squeeze in the 8 GU Pumpkin Spice gels and whisk in the ½ cup cold water until completely smooth. 3. Whisk the base: Mix in the 2 scoops of the GU Vanilla Roctane Recovery Mix. Let it sit for 2 minutes so the foam settles. Then whisk in the 3 eggs until uniform. 4. Combine remaining ingredients: Add the 4 tablespoons cornstarch, 2 tablespoons melted butter, ¼ teaspoon salt, and optional cinnamon, whisking until smooth and pourable. (If the batter looks thicker than heavy pancake batter, whisk in 1 to 2 tablespoons of extra water). 5. Initial high-heat bake: Pour the filling into the unbaked pie crust. Bake at 400°F for 12 minutes to set the bottom crust. 6. Finish baking gently: Without opening the oven door, reduce the temperature to 325°F. Bake for another 30 to 40 minutes, until the outer 2 inches of filling are puffed and set, while the very center still jiggles like gelatin when gently nudged. (If the crust edges brown too rapidly, cover them loosely with foil). 7. Cool and chill: Remove the pie from the oven and let it cool completely to room temperature on a wire rack (about 1.5 to 2 hours). Transfer to the refrigerator and chill for at least 4 hours (or overnight) so the cornstarch fully sets before slicing. I opted for overnight so it would be ready for my morning heat session on the trainer.

Jason Griffin is Bicycling's Senior Health and Fitness Editor, bringing more than a decade of fitness experience and years in the cycling industry to every story. A former personal trainer and bike shop manager, he's lined up for crits, tackled enduros, but prefers getting lost on multi-day bikepacking adventures. Lately though, his toughest balancing act has been fitting trainer rides between family life and the next adventure.

‘Just a Guy With a Boat on His Head’: He’s Running 52 Marathons in 52 Weeks—While Carrying a Canoe Every Step

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1037 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Runnersworld

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that getting to the Philadelphia Marathon on November 22 proved an endurance event of its own for Travis Meier.
  • And yes, the canoe made it through the entire race without ever touching water.
  • “Coming from Minnesota, I can't just throw a boat in an overhead compartment," Meier told Runner's World.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that getting to the Philadelphia Marathon on November 22 proved an endurance event of its own for Travis Meier. The 38-year-old Minneapolis resident flew into Hartford, Connecticut, drove three hours into the Adirondack Mountains to pick up a canoe, then spent another five hours behind the wheel getting to Philadelphia. This was all before tackling Sunday’s 26.2 miles with the boat balanced over his head.

And yes, the canoe made it through the entire race without ever touching water.

“Coming from Minnesota, I can't just throw a boat in an overhead compartment," Meier told Runner's World. "It was a logistical nightmare: where to keep it, where to sneak it into the race, and how people would react to it.".

Industry observers note that despite the travel headaches, Meier came away from Philadelphia with his second personal record in as many weeks. It was another step in his latest undertaking: 52 marathons in 52 weeks, each while carrying a canoe, to raise awareness about protecting the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness in northern Minnesota.

It has been revealed that meier, who manages a distillery when he isn't hauling boats around, wasn't exactly a seasoned runner when all this started. His introduction to the sport came through the Red Bull Urban Portage, an event that involved carrying a boat through downtown Minneapolis before paddling along the Mississippi River.

In a recent development, “I was really bad at paddling, but I could outrun people,” he recalled. Before the event, he bought a Northstar ADK canoe off Craigslist with every intention of selling it once the race was over. Instead, it found a home on his garage wall and managed to stick around for another year. Eventually, he started entering more races with it.

Industry observers note that that eventually brought him to Minnesota's Ely Marathon in 2023, where he completed his first-ever 26.2-mile race while carrying a canoe. Since then, he's run only one conventional marathon without a boat, and what started solely as a personal experiment gradually became an opportunity to draw attention to a place he'd loved for years.

The Boundary Waters, a wilderness area known for its lakes, forests, and extensive canoe routes, has been at the center of a contentious debate over proposed mining operations. Federal protections restricting mining in the surrounding watershed were rolled back earlier this year, a development that particularly frustrated Meier.

Sources indicate that "I've been to many remote places on this earth, and very few have its caliber of perfect,” he noted. “So why would someone want to mess it up?".

According to recent reports, meier had been toying with the idea of running 52 marathons in 52 weeks ever since reading about Dane Rauschenberg, who accomplished the feat in 2006. With the ongoing fight over protections for the Boundary Waters, he had his reason to give it a shot, bringing his canoe as a form of protest to May’s Taco Bell 50K. It got people asking questions, which was exactly what he wanted, and gave him encouragement to keep showing up at races with a boat on his head.

Of course, carrying a canoe for more than four hours at a time comes with some challenges, particularly when Mother Nature gets involved.

According to recent reports, during the Mankato Marathon in Minnesota, Meier battled 30mph winds along a ridge beside a cornfield. Mile 14 alone took him nearly 22 minutes, as his canoe repeatedly caught the wind and spun him around like a kite.

It has been revealed that at one point, Meier turned to a few supporters witnessing him get thrown around and asked, “When's the point of insanity?” He sent them ahead to see if the wind conditions were better ahead in the valley. Luckily, the gusts let up enough, sparing him a repeat trip through that nightmare.

The spectators in Philadelphia offered a different kind of entertainment, with plenty to say about the guy running a marathon with a canoe on his head.

Around mile three, Meier encountered a young girl who appeared scared by the enormous object approaching her. He knelt down, giving her enough confidence to return his high-five.

"Grandmas confess their love to me, and I don't know why," he said of his interactions with spectators, adding that Philadelphia set a record for the number of phallic jokes he heard along the course.

The jokes are part of the experience, and the attention is ultimately what he's hoping for. Meier remarked fellow runners often approach him after a race to discuss the Boundary Waters and the larger problem of protecting public lands. He's also seen Instagram comments from people who knew little about the area before coming across his videos.

"They may not know anything, but they've at least gotten a 10,000-foot view of the BWCA," he stated.

The running community has helped make the challenge possible, with sponsors pitching in for race entries and shoes while Meier covers the remaining expenses. He's even promised to refund their donations if he doesn't complete the challenge.

"My integrity is everything,” he remarked, “even though I'm not a manufacturer, just a guy with a boat on his head.”.

According to recent reports, his biggest sacrifice so far has been giving up so much of his free time. Between a full-time job, travel, recovery, and the weekly races, there’s no room for a vacation abroad. He has considered tackling back-to-back marathons to create some breathing room. His body hasn't agreed to the arrangement.

As for what would make all 52 races worthwhile, Meier has a specific outcome in mind: permanent legislation protecting the Boundary Waters. Here’s the good news: proposals exist in both the House of Representatives and Senate. Even so, he knows that may be a tall order. But his presence—and effort—are creating awareness.

"If it doesn't happen, which it likely won't, at least the effort started conversations about our public lands," he said.

According to recent reports, sean Abrams was the Senior Editor, Growth and Engagement at Men’s Health. He’s a former hip hop dancer who likes long walks on the beach and large glasses of tequila. You can find his previous work at Maxim, Elite Daily, and AskMen.

In Praise of the Charity Ride, One of the Most Underrated Ways to Tackle Your First Century—or Any Substantial Cycling Goal

💡 Key Takeaways
